intended_paths.status: staging-only handoff; no canonical path is claimed and no other package's files were touched

implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX (aliased into EDI at 0x00642710 and never moved back; ECX is clobbered by the lookup calls and never reloaded, because the body reaches the receiver only through EDI); exactly ONE ordinary stack argument, consumed by the callee at 0x00642816 / 0x0064282b / 0x00642831 (RET 0x4). That argument is the object the body appends to: 0x0064271e reads it with MOV ESI,[ESP+0x18] at ESP = entry-20, i.e. entry+4, and the body never reads it again except through ESI. The frame walk in mechanics.frame_resolution is what fixes the count at one rather than two: the only other frame slot the body writes, at entry-4, is the slot PUSH ECX itself filled with the receiver, so the receiver is never recovered from a slot and no second argument exists. Ghidra's decompilation prints two parameters because it models the hidden receiver as param_1; the listing is followed here.
implementation.return_type_justification: The listing writes ONLY the low byte of the return register on every path: XOR AL,AL at 0x0064282e, MOV AL,0x1 at 0x00642812 and MOV AL,0x1 at 0x00642827. The upper three bytes of EAX are therefore undefined on all three exits, and one byte is the width the machine fixes. This is option (a) of the wave-1 guidance: a type that is TRUE OF THE LISTING, with the disagreement against the record recorded in unresolved_questions. It is NOT option (b) void -- the bytes genuinely produce a value, and three separate instructions produce it. The canonical ABI record's own return claim is the machine-vocabulary string "integral_in_EAX" (abi.return_semantics, and abi_derived inference RT2 register_class "integral"), which is a claim about the register rather than about a C type; no C++ type can be spelled to equal it, so RETURN SEMANTICS is expected to WARN and that WARN is not chased. No typedef was invented to win the string comparison.
implementation.receiver_model: an OPAQUE 12-byte run. bounds_only is true on the machine-derived receiver record (offsets [8], register ECX, shape R-DIRECT, written_through 0, confidence INFERRED), so NO struct member is declared for either displacement the body reaches. 0x04 (the lookup base, 0x00642710) and 0x08 (the gate word, 0x00642701) are named constexprs in the header and reached through word_at()/pointer arithmetic in the body, exactly as the wave-1 guidance prescribes. The record does not enumerate 0x04 at all; the complete 114-instruction listing is the better witness and the model accounts for 0x04 from it. The same treatment is applied to the argument object, whose two reached words are kVectorCursorDisplacement (0x04) and kVectorCapacityDisplacement (0x08).
implementation.dispatch_model: none: the body has no indirect transfer (0 in the listing, 0 in abi_derived.dispatch) and the model declares no slot boundary. The twelve vtable references this record carries are recorded for the integrator in evidence.vtable_associations_not_used_as_evidence and are deliberately NOT modelled, because the body never reads a word at any object's +0x00 through a table and naming a slot would be a claim the body does not make.
implementation.dependency_note: both direct callees are declared extern in the package header and defined as observers in the package's own model test; no other package's header is included. 0x00556140 and 0x004558a0 are not owned by this package and this package asserts nothing about them beyond what their own instruction bytes fix: their terminators, their argument shape, their argument order and the four effects of 0x004558a0 on its receiver that the test reproduces.

The header additionally compiles clean as its own translation unit under the same flags. See validation.wpedantic_note for the one flag this package is NOT clean under, and validation.mutation_checking for the eleven injected defects and their outcomes.

target_state: implemented staging handoff. The body, both direct callees' contracts and the whole stack frame were re-derived from the image bytes for this package; the 308 bytes at 0x00642700..0x00642833 decode to the committed 114-instruction listing instruction for instruction and stop one byte into the INT3 padding at 0x00642834, so the committed record's extent is CORRECT and no listing correction is needed or claimed. The body's shape is one gate word plus FIVE UNROLLED copies of one append, and the frame walk settles the argument count at one -- which is the fact the committed ABI record itself abstained from, listing 'flow_not_modelled: the linear ESP walk ends at +24' and 'sret_vs_out_param'. Both abstentions are resolved here against the bytes: with each callee's own terminator settling the stack, the frame balances to exactly one argument word on all three exits, and the argument is written through rather than written to, so it is an append target and not a hidden struct return. STATIC is expected at 8 PASS and 1 WARN: the single structural WARN is RETURN SEMANTICS, and it is a property of the record's machine-vocabulary return string, not a defect in the source (see implementation.return_type_justification). EVIDENCE COVERAGE is expected to WARN at 10 of 17 categories and RUNTIME remains GATED at 0 with nothing attempted. See validation.observed and validation.expected.

The committed record agrees on all four extent numbers (body_start 0x00642700, body_end 0x00642833, body_span_bytes 308, size_bytes 308) and abi_derived.parse agrees at declared_count 114, unparsed 0, degraded false. NO discrepancy to report.
function_extent.file_offset_note: the .text section's file offset is its RVA minus 0xc00 in this image. That was measured by decoding 0x00642700 at both RVA 0x242700 and 0x241b00 and comparing against the committed listing: at 0x242700 the bytes decode to unrelated code (an `imul edi,[ebx],0x64731050`), and at 0x241b00 they decode to this body exactly.

observed_original_abi.receiver_alias: EDI (LEA EDI,[ECX+0x4] at 0x00642710; every receiver access after the gate goes through EDI, and EDI is pushed again and popped again without ever being moved back to ECX)
observed_original_abi.stack_argument_1: entry_ESP+0x4 -- the object the body appends to. Read exactly once, with MOV ESI,[ESP+0x18] at 0x0064271e while ESP = entry-20, and used only through ESI afterwards. Ghidra's param_2 / iVar4. The committed ABI record reports this same slot (ordinary_stack_argument_slots [entry_ESP+0x4]) but annotates it read:false, which its own abstained_because explains: a linear ESP walk that does not settle each call's stack effect cannot place a read that happens while two cdecl argument words are still live. The byte walk places it at entry+4 exactly, and the committed slot is therefore RIGHT and its read flag is what the walk could not see.
observed_original_abi.return_type_machine_claim: the canonical record says integral_in_EAX; the listing writes AL only. See implementation.return_type_justification and unresolved_questions item 1.
observed_original_abi.callee_conventions: each fixed by the callee's own last bytes, read from the image: 0x00556140 ends a bare C3 at 0x0055620a, so it pops nothing and is cdecl with two caller-cleaned words (the caller drops them at 0x00642725 and its four siblings with ADD ESP,0x8); 0x004558a0 ends C2 08 00 at 0x00455ad4 and stashes ECX at 0x004558a7, so it is __thiscall with two callee-owned words. Both are re-derived in mechanics.callee_contracts.
observed_original_abi.evidence_level: ABI_INFERRED (abi_derived.verdict = ABI_INFERRED, conventions.confidence = INFERRED, completeness = CORE_RESOLVED, conflicts = [])
observed_original_abi.ghidra_prototype: undefined __thiscall FUN_00642700(int param_1, int param_2) -- the committed ghidra_function record carries return_type 'undefined', return_type_resolved false and parameter_count 0, and the decompilation prints two int parameters because it modelled the hidden receiver as param_1. Nothing in the listing uses EDX at all, and the receiver is demonstrably in ECX (0x00642701 dereferences it before any definite write, and 0x00642710 forms the base from it).

mechanics.body_shape: compare the receiver's word at +0x08 against one fixed literal and return false if it differs; otherwise append the result of five hash lookups (0x00556140 called with the receiver's +0x04 and five distinct 32-bit literals, in that order) to a caller-supplied four-byte-element vector, once per lookup, and return true. Each append either writes the element in place -- advancing the vector's cursor word FIRST and only then null-testing and storing -- or delegates to 0x004558a0, which receives the cursor by value and the ADDRESS of the value and leaves the cursor word untouched.
mechanics.unrolled_not_looped: there is no loop and no backward branch. The five appends are 0x00642713-0x0064274c, 0x0064274c-0x00642781, 0x00642781-0x006427b6, 0x006427b6-0x006427eb and 0x006427eb-0x0064280d, each a full copy of the other. The model carries the same duplication rather than factoring it into a helper the listing does not have, so the transfer sequence of one call is ten transfers long (five lookups and up to five reallocations) and a loop-shaped reconstruction would be a different body. The model test's D case is what keeps the ORDER of those transfers refutable.

frame_resolution.method: one walk of ESP through the whole body, with each callee's own terminator settling the stack after every call -- the callee's pop of the RETURN ADDRESS included, which is the step that makes the walk balance. Entry ESP is 0 in the walk. The walk is PATH-SENSITIVE, and it has to be: a linear walk drifts by four bytes per reallocation, because the slow arm's LEA/PUSH/PUSH/CALL group is +4 net only once 0x004558a0's RET 0x8 is counted. That drift is exactly the committed record's abstention 'flow_not_modelled: the linear ESP walk ends at +24, so the listing is not one path'.

settled_callee_effects.0x00556140: PUSH imm (-4) + PUSH EDI (-4) + CALL (-4) + bare C3 pops the return address (+4) + ADD ESP,0x8 (+8) = 0. Two words in, two words out, caller-cleaned.
settled_callee_effects.0x004558a0: LEA (0) + PUSH EAX (-4) + PUSH ECX (-4) + CALL (-4) + RET 0x8 pops the return address and two words (+12) = 0. Two words in, two words out, callee-cleaned.

frame_resolution.corroboration: three independent agreements, and they are the reason the argument count is one. (1) 0x0064271e reads [ESP+0x18] with ESP = entry-20 on BOTH arms of the first append (the walk gives entry-20 there whichever arm is taken, because the two argument words are still live at that point), and entry-20+0x18 = entry+4, the single argument slot the record names. (2) The value slot 0x00642728 writes, [ESP+0x8] with ESP = entry-12, is entry-4 -- the slot 0x00642700's PUSH ECX itself just filled with the receiver -- which is Ghidra's local_4 and is why the receiver is never recovered from the frame afterwards. (3) All three exits close: the epilogue's three POPs run from ESP = entry-12 back to entry, and RET 0x4 lands on entry+4, which is exactly the caller's ESP after its own push of one argument.

slots.entry+4: the ordinary stack argument -- the append target. The body overwrites it from 0x0064275d onward (see below) and never reads it again.
slots.entry-4: the receiver, pushed at 0x00642700 and then OVERWRITTEN by the first lookup's result at 0x00642728. Never recovered; the receiver is reached only through EDI from 0x00642710 onward.

frame_resolution.value_slot_is_not_constant: the per-append value slot is at TWO different addresses and the model does not pretend otherwise. Iteration one forms it as [ESP+0x8] with ESP = entry-12, i.e. entry-4. Iterations two through five form it as [ESP+0x10] with ESP = entry-12, i.e. entry+4 -- the CALLER'S OWN ARGUMENT WORD, which the body has not read since 0x0064271e and which it therefore destroys. The model uses one local for the value in every iteration, because the incoming argument is dead after 0x0064271e and no address the body computes is ever handed back out in a way a caller can observe. This is stated and asserted NOWHERE: asserting the model's single address would be a claim the machine contradicts, so it lives here and in the .cpp annotation only.
frame_resolution.bytes_destroyed_beyond_the_frame: one caller-visible side effect the argument slot makes observable: on any path that reaches 0x0064275d, the word at entry+4 -- the argument the caller pushed -- is overwritten with a lookup result. The argument is dead to the body, but it is not dead to a caller that reads its own argument slot back. No record fixes whether any caller does; nothing is claimed.

receiver_displacement.0x08: read at 0x00642701 (CMP dword ptr [ECX+0x8],0x2b978c46) and nowhere else. The word is compared EQUALITY against one literal and is the only thing the gate tests. The machine-derived receiver record enumerates this displacement.
receiver_displacement.0x04: formed as an ADDRESS at 0x00642710 (LEA EDI,[ECX+0x4]) and pushed as the first argument of 0x00556140 five times (0x00642718, 0x00642751, 0x00642786, 0x006427bb, 0x006427f0). The body never LOADS this word and never dereferences it. The machine-derived receiver record does NOT enumerate 0x04 and declares itself bounds_only; the complete listing is the better witness and the model accounts for 0x04 from it.

de_registration_corroboration.claim: the word at the receiver's +0x08 is the SECOND word of the object the body forms at the receiver's +0x04, and 0x00556140 is the function that checks it.
de_registration_corroboration.evidence: 0x0055614d MOV EAX,[EBP+0x8] takes the callee's first argument; 0x00556150 CMP DWORD PTR [EAX+0x4],0x2b978c46 compares the SECOND word of that object against the very literal this body compares its own +0x08 against at 0x00642701. Since this body hands the callee the receiver's +0x04 (0x00642710), the two reads are the same address and the two literals are the same value.
de_registration_corroboration.consequence: the receiver's +0x08 is a TYPE-IDENTITY word of a two-word object, not a magic of the receiver itself, and the same literal is checked twice on every one of the five calls. The model expresses this as kSourceLookupBaseDisplacement 0x04 and kDescriptorGateDisplacement 0x04 rather than as a guess about a class layout.
de_registration_corroboration.second_accepted_identity: 0x0055615c CMP DWORD PTR [ECX+0x4],0x3d97a8e4 is the other identity 0x00556140 accepts, and this body NEVER tests it. So the receiver this body runs on is one of at least two flavours and the body is flavour-specific. No record says what either literal is; nothing is claimed.

argument_object_displacement.0x04: the cursor. LOADED at 0x00642722 and at 0x00642757, 0x0064278c, 0x006427c1, 0x006427f6 -- re-read before EVERY append, never cached across one. WRITTEN at 0x00642734 and at 0x00642769, 0x0064279e, 0x006427d3, 0x00642808, on the in-place arm only. STORED THROUGH at 0x0064273b and its four siblings, guarded by TEST ECX,ECX at 0x00642737 and its four siblings. It is a POINTER held in a word: the machine loads a plain dword and then writes through it, so the model reads a Word and reinterprets it as an address and never dereferences it on the body's behalf.
argument_object_displacement.0x08: the capacity, read at 0x0064272c and at 0x00642761, 0x00642796, 0x006427cb, 0x00642800 and compared against the cursor with an UNSIGNED, STRICT-LESS test. Never stored through by this body, so it is a bound and not a pointer. The model test drives a signed/unsigned disagreement (cursor 0x80000000 against capacity 0x40000000) to keep that from being read as a value.
argument_object_displacement.0x00: touched by 0x004558a0 only -- 0x004558b0 CMP EDX,[EAX+0x8] reads the capacity, 0x004558f6 MOV ECX,[EDX-0x4] reads the last element, 0x00455ab6/0x00455abe writes the begin word, 0x00455ac7/0x00455acd writes the capacity word. This body NEVER reads or writes it. It is recorded as a value (kVectorBeginDisplacement) and not declared, and the model test byte-compares the word to keep that falsifiable.
argument_object_displacement.element_stride: 4 bytes, from 0x00642731 LEA EDX,[ECX+0x4] and the five MOV DWORD PTR [ECX],EAX stores that go with it. The model does the arithmetic in BYTES (uintptr_t + stride), never as `Word* + stride`: the first draft of this model made exactly that mistake -- `Word* + 4` is four ELEMENTS, sixteen bytes -- and the model test caught it on the first run. The comment at the store says so.
argument_object_displacement.shape: a growable sequence of 4-byte elements with the cursor at +0x04 and the capacity at +0x08 is the layout 0x004558a0's own body reads and writes (0x004558b0/0x004558b3 for the cursor and the capacity, 0x00455961/0x00455967 for the one-element advance, 0x00455ac7/0x00455acd for the rebuilt capacity), and the 0x14 divide at 0x00455a81 and the 0x14 multiply-back at 0x00455a63 are on a different path of that callee. This body itself never divides, so it fixes the stride only as 'the amount 0x00642731 adds', which is 4 bytes; the callee's own element-count arithmetic is what corroborates that a 4-byte element is the right unit and not an accident. No type, class or STL container is claimed for the object.

mechanics.control_flow: eleven conditional branches, every target inside the recovered body span 0x00642700..0x00642833, plus four intra-procedural JMPs (0x0064273d, 0x00642772, 0x006427a7, 0x006427dc) that skip a store and land back on the next append. Full list in the .cpp header. The branch graph is a tree: no unconditional backward branch, no loop, no address reached twice on any path, so no state is carried between two visits of any instruction and the model needs no loop invariant.
mechanics.arm_decision: per append, the arm is chosen by the UNSIGNED compare `cursor >= capacity` (JNC after CMP ECX,[ESI+0x8]), so the in-place arm is reachable only when cursor < capacity STRICTLY. On the in-place arm the cursor word is advanced FIRST (0x00642731/0x00642734) and the element is written only if the cursor is not null (0x00642737/0x00642739/0x0064273b), so a null cursor still moves the cursor by one element. On the slow arm nothing in this body is written: the cursor word still holds exactly the value 0x004558a0 is handed, which is the point the model test samples at the moment of the call.
mechanics.write_ordering: the in-place arm's order is INVERTED relative to the intuitive source order and the listing is followed exactly: bump the cursor word, then null-test, then store. A reconstruction that stored first and bumped second would be observably different on the null-cursor path only in intermediate states, and observably different on the slow path not at all -- so the model test drives the null-cursor path on every append and on the fifth append alone (case G and G2), where 0x0064280d's jump goes to the SHARED TRUE TAIL rather than to a sixth append.
mechanics.exits: three exits, two values. False only from 0x0064282e (XOR AL,AL / POP ECX / RET 0x4), reached only by the gate. True from 0x00642812 (the fifth append's in-place arm, which hoists the first epilogue POP above the element store so the result byte can be written one instruction sooner) and from 0x00642827 (the shared tail, reached from 0x0064280d and from the fifth append's slow arm). The body therefore reports true even when all five appends reallocated and even when all five had a null cursor, and the model test drives both.
mechanics.receiver_writes: NONE. The 114 instructions contain no store through ECX or through EDI. The model test byte-compares the whole 0x40-byte receiver run across three mixed calls and once more on the failing gate. The only two stores the body makes into a caller-supplied object are the cursor word (in place) and, through it, the element itself.
mechanics.globals: none. No instruction in the 114 names a data-segment address, and the xref export records no data reference for this target (dependencies.data_reference_count 0). The nearest thing to a global is the frame slot 0x00556146 that 0x00556140 zeroes, which is that callee's own business.

0x00556140.convention: cdecl. The body ends a bare C3 at 0x0055620a, so it pops no arguments, and it drops each of its own callees' arguments itself (0x00556172 and 0x005561df, both ADD ESP,0x4). ECX is never read.
0x00556140.argument_order: descriptor FIRST, key SECOND. The pushes run the key (0x00642713 and its four siblings) then the descriptor (0x00642718 and its four siblings), and the callee's own reads agree: 0x0055614d MOV EAX,[EBP+0x8] is the descriptor and 0x005561e2 CMP EAX,[EBP+0xc] is the key. The descriptor is the ADDRESS of the receiver's +0x04, formed once by 0x00642710 and pushed five times; the body never loads that word and never dereferences it.
0x00556140.key_constants: 0xa426730b (0x00642713), 0xad56080c (0x0064274c), 0xf71fa311 (0x00642781), 0xbeb528cb (0x006427b6), 0x2db6dad3 (0x006427eb) -- one per call, in that order, and never reused.
0x00556140.return: one word, 0x00556204 reads the frame slot 0x00556146 zeroed and 0x00556207 hands it back in EAX. It is a pointer or null, and THIS body only ever STORES it: the five `MOV dword ptr [ESP+0x..],EAX` and the five `MOV dword ptr [ECX],EAX` are its whole use. The model test drives a return value of 0x00000001 -- an address that is not mapped on this host -- and asserts it is stored verbatim, so a body that dereferenced the result would fault rather than quietly pass.
0x00556140.de_registration: 0x00556150 CMP DWORD PTR [EAX+0x4],0x2b978c46 is the same word and the same literal this body tests at 0x00642701. See mechanics.de_registration_corroboration.
0x00556140.return_is_never_null_tested: the body does not test the lookup's return on any of the five calls. A null result is appended like any other value. The model test does not plant a null result, because nothing in the machine distinguishes it and driving it would only test the test; the claim made here is the narrower one, that the listing contains no test of EAX between the call and the store.

0x004558a0.at: 0x00642747, 0x0064277c, 0x006427b1, 0x006427e6, 0x00642821 -- the slow arm of each of the five appends, and only there
0x004558a0.convention: __thiscall. PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / SUB ESP,0x60 / PUSH ESI at 0x004558a0..0x004558a6, ECX stashed at 0x004558a7, and POP ESI / MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP / RET 0x8 at 0x00455ad0..0x00455ad4, so it owns its two argument words.
0x004558a0.argument_order: cursor FIRST, value SECOND. The pushes run the value's ADDRESS (0x00642743 and its four siblings, each preceded by a LEA) and then the cursor (0x00642744 and its four siblings), and the callee's own reads agree: 0x004558bc MOV EAX,[EBP+0x8] is the cursor and it is STORED THROUGH at 0x00455959, while 0x004558bf/0x00455957 reads the SECOND word as the value's source. So insert_at_end(self, cursor, &value), with the value passed BY ADDRESS.
0x004558a0.receiver: the ARGUMENT object, not this body's receiver. 0x00642745, 0x0064277a, 0x006427af, 0x006427e4 and 0x0064281f all do MOV ECX,ESI, and ESI is the stack argument throughout.
0x004558a0.effects_reproduced_by_the_test: the model test's observer reproduces exactly four effects, each read off this callee's own bytes: 0x00455957/0x00455959 store the value at the cursor handed over; 0x00455961/0x00455967 advance the cursor word by one element; 0x00455ab6/0x00455abe rewrite the begin word; 0x00455ac7/0x00455acd rebuild the capacity word. Nothing else of the callee is modelled and nothing else is claimed.
0x004558a0.return: dead on every arm. After 0x00642747, 0x0064277c, 0x006427b1 and 0x006427e6 the next thing to write EAX is the next lookup's own return, and after 0x00642821 it is 0x00642827 MOV AL,0x1. The declared return type is void and the model test asserts nothing about it.

mechanics.decompiler_agreement: the live decompilation agrees with the model on the body shape and disagrees on the frame. It prints `__thiscall FUN_00642700(int param_1,int param_2)` -- its param_1 is this body's ECX receiver and its param_2 is the stack argument, so it has shifted both up by one and reports two parameters where the frame carries one. Its `local_4` is this body's entry-4 slot (the receiver's own word on the way in, the first lookup's result on the way out) and its `iVar1` is the receiver + 4, the descriptor; both are followed here. Its capacity test, `if (piVar2 < *(int **)(param_2 + 8))`, is the same unsigned condition 0x0064272f/0x0064272c read the other way round, and it places the null guard before the store, which the listing also does. Nothing in its output contradicts the model on any value, constant, displacement, argument order or callee.
mechanics.vtable_note: this body is an entry in twelve tables, which is what makes it a virtual function and is the only thing those records establish. The body's own data-side xrefs are at 0x013ff6d4, 0x014627e4, 0x0147ca84, 0x0147cb4c, 0x0148911c, 0x0148943c and 0x00dd1209, and the tables at 0x013ff648, 0x013ff6ac and 0x01462764 are the same ones the record names as the match basis for the reconstructed neighbours 0x00641400, 0x00641460, 0x00641770, 0x006417b0, 0x006417c0, 0x00641810, 0x00641820 and 0x00641850, all of which the research queue names Sporepedia::cSPAssetDataOTDB::*. That is why the header's type is spelled Sporepedia* and the class NAME is left out. NONE of it is modelled: the body contains no indirect transfer (0 in the listing and 0 in abi_derived.dispatch) and it never reads a word at any object's +0x00, so naming a slot or a base offset would be a claim the body does not make. The addresses are recorded here, in the header, and nowhere in the function span.

return_semantics.kind: boolean byte in the low half of the return register
return_semantics.value: 1 when the receiver's word at +0x08 equals 0x2b978c46, 0 otherwise, on every path that reaches an exit. The side effects are the five appends and nothing else. There is no path that reports false for any reason other than the gate, and no path that reports false after a partial append sequence.
return_semantics.width: one byte. The three writing instructions are XOR AL,AL (0x0064282e) and MOV AL,0x1 twice (0x00642812, 0x00642827); the upper three bytes of EAX are undefined on all three exits and the declared type is bool so that no wider value is claimed.
return_semantics.disagreement_with_the_record: abi.return_semantics and abi_derived inference RT2 both say 'integral_in_EAX' / register_class 'integral', and the ghidra_function record says return_type 'undefined' with return_type_resolved false. A boolean byte is integral in EAX in the loose sense, so the record is not refuted -- but it is a claim about the register and not about a C type, and no C++ spelling of it can be compared for equality by the validator. return_semantics.ownership: the body acquires and releases nothing. It hands the receiver's +0x04 address to 0x00556140 five times and the argument object to 0x004558a0 up to five times; whether either callee takes a reference is not established by any record for this target and is not claimed. 0x00556140's own body shows a call through a table word at +0x00 twice around its search (0x0055618e and 0x00556202), which is the shape of an acquire/release pair, but that is the callee's business and it is recorded here as an observation, not as a claim about this body's ownership.

unresolved_questions: The canonical ABI record's return claim is the machine-vocabulary string 'integral_in_EAX' (abi.return_semantics; abi_derived inference RT2 register_class 'integral'), and the ghidra_function record says return_type 'undefined' with return_type_resolved false. The listing writes only AL, so this package declares bool -- the width the machine fixes -- which is option (a) of the wave-1 guidance. The consequence is that RETURN SEMANTICS compares the strings 'bool' and 'integral_in_EAX' and WARNs, and no honest declaration can make that comparison succeed. Declaring void is not available (three instructions produce a value) and inventing a typedef named after the machine phrase would be a validator hack, so the WARN is reported and not chased. This is the package's only structural WARN.

The committed record's abi.abstained_because gives two reasons not to trust its own argument analysis -- 'flow_not_modelled: the linear ESP walk ends at +24, so the listing is not one path' and 'sret_vs_out_param: entry slot 0 is written through a pointer' -- and the byte walk here resolves both. It is worth recording that they are resolved by WALKING each callee's own terminator rather than by the listing alone: with 0x004558a0's `RET 0x8` counted as 12 bytes net (return address plus two words) rather than 8, the frame drifts four bytes per reallocation and never balances, which reproduces the record's +24. Anyone re-deriving this frame should use mechanics.frame_resolution.settled_callee_effects, which is the part that is easy to get wrong.

The committed record annotates its single stack argument 'read: false'. The byte walk puts the read at 0x0064271e, MOV ESI,[ESP+0x18] with ESP = entry-20, i.e. entry+4, which is the record's own slot. So the slot is right and the read flag is what a linear walk could not see. If a downstream tool relies on that flag it will conclude the body never touches its argument, which is false.

What 0x2b978c46 IS, is not established. It is the word at the receiver's +0x08, the second word of the two-word descriptor at the receiver's +0x04, and 0x00556140 checks it (0x00556150) before doing anything. That 0x00556140 accepts a SECOND identity, 0x3d97a8e4 (0x0055615c), which this body never tests, means the receiver is one of at least two flavours and this body is flavour-specific -- but no record in this repository says what either literal denotes, and nothing is claimed.

What the five literals are is not established either. They are passed one per call to 0x00556140, which uses the second argument in a linear search (0x005561b9..0x005561ef) comparing each candidate against it (0x005561e2), so they behave as lookup KEYS. Whether they are Sporepedia type-property ids, hash values, or the low 32 bits of string ids is not established, and the model claims only that five distinct 32-bit literals are passed in a fixed order.

What the ARGUMENT OBJECT is is not established beyond its two reached words. This body reads a cursor at +0x04 and a capacity at +0x08 and advances the cursor by 4 bytes; 0x004558a0's own body reads and writes +0x00, +0x04 and +0x08 of it and rebuilds the capacity from a 0x14 divide. That is the layout of a growable sequence of 4-byte elements and it is very likely a std::vector<unsigned int>, but the model deliberately does not say so: this binary has no MSVC RTTI, the record's types category is unavailable, and naming a container would be a claim no record carries. The stride is fixed as 'the amount 0x00642731 adds', which is 4 bytes; the element-count arithmetic that corroborates a 4-byte ELEMENT is the callee's, not this body's.

Is the caller-visible destruction of the argument slot load-bearing? On any path that reaches 0x0064275d this body overwrites the caller's own argument word (entry+4) with a lookup result -- the vector pointer the caller pushed is destroyed. The argument is dead to the body, but a caller that read its own argument slot back would see a lookup result. No record establishes whether any caller does, and the model does not assert the machine's slot aliasing at all (see mechanics.frame_resolution.value_slot_is_not_constant).

Is 0x00642700 a virtual function with any DIRECT caller at all? The record carries seven data-side xrefs, all of which are this body's own address inside twelve tables, so the entry is a virtual function; no direct-call xref is recorded in either direction. Whether some other image, a mod, or a vtable reached only at run time calls it directly is not established here.

What the class actually is. The Sporepedia association is real (twelve tables, and the tables at 0x013ff648, 0x013ff6ac and 0x01462764 are the same ones the record names as the match basis for eight reconstructed neighbours the research queue names Sporepedia::cSPAssetDataOTDB::*) but the record's own class_type is null and the name is not written anywhere in this package. The header spells the types Sporepedia* and stops there.

The three appends' and five appends' frame slots mean the body reuses its own argument word as a scratch register, which is legal for the callee but is a fact about the CALLER's stack that a caller with a live argument slot would notice. Combined with the previous item this is the one place where a faithful reconstruction of the body could differ observably from the original in a way a caller could observe, and it is left unmodelled on purpose.

conditions: The original process is driven to an object whose word at +0x08 is 0x2b978c46, with a vector argument that has room for five 4-byte elements, and the five appended words are compared against the reconstruction's.
A trace records ECX, the descriptor address in EDI and the argument pointer in ESI at 0x0064271e, to confirm entry-20 for ESP at that instruction and therefore entry+4 for the argument.
A trace records the stack pointer at every one of the ten calls and the value 0x004558a0 leaves in EAX, to confirm the frame balances to entry+4 on all three returns.

A trace is taken with the vector's capacity exactly equal to its cursor, so the slow arm runs on all five appends, and the five values 0x004558a0 produces are compared against the five the body passed as &value.

A trace is taken with the cursor word set to 0x80000000 and the capacity word to 0x40000000, to confirm the compare at 0x0064272c and its four siblings is unsigned and grows rather than appends in place.

A trace is taken with the cursor null, to confirm the cursor word still advances by 4 and the element store is skipped, on every append and on the fifth append alone through 0x0064280d's jump to the shared tail.
The byte left in AL at each of the three returns is compared against the reconstruction's bool, and the upper three bytes of EAX are confirmed to be unobservable to the original callers.

validation.model_test: plain int main() with explicit checks, no framework and no external dependency. Both direct callees are defined in the test as observers that record their arguments, sample the vector's cursor word at the moment of the call, and return or write chosen values. Eleven cases: A the gate word's displacement and four different wrong values plus two decoy copies of the right value at the neighbouring displacements, with the argument object byte-compared on the failing gate; B the whole chain in place -- the five literals in order, the descriptor as the first argument on all five calls, the five results in the arena, the cursor five elements on, the capacity and the +0x00 word untouched; C five reallocations -- receiver identity, cursor-by-value versus value-by-address, the cursor word at the call still equal to what was handed over, and the arena holding the five results contiguously; D a mixed sequence with the arms interleaving, compared as a shape; E the capacity boundary from both sides, cursor == capacity reallocating and cursor == capacity - 1 appending in place, with the per-append cursor sample confirming the first append landed exactly on the capacity; F signed versus unsigned (0x80000000 against 0x40000000); G and G2 the null cursor on every append and on the fifth append alone, with the cursor still advanced and nothing stored; H the receiver byte-unchanged across three mixed calls and on the failing gate; I the argument object's +0x00 and +0x0c byte-unchanged, with a decoy word planted at +0x0c; J a lookup result of 0x00000001, an address not mapped on this host, stored verbatim on all five appends; K two calls in a row with different observer results and nothing carried between them.

mutation_checking.survivors: none of the sixteen injected defects survived. Two of them were real defects in this package's own first draft, and both are annotated at the place in the source where they were fixed so a reader can see what the test bought.
mutation_checking.known_limits: The value-slot aliasing is not asserted (see mechanics.frame_resolution.value_slot_is_not_constant): the machine writes iterations two through five into the CALLER'S argument word and the model uses one local for the value in every iteration, so a reconstruction can be neither refuted nor credited for that aliasing. Nothing asserts EAX's upper three bytes, because the declared type is one byte wide and the machine leaves them undefined. The grow observer's capacity arithmetic is scaffolding chosen by the test, not a claim about 0x004558a0: only the four effects read off that callee's own bytes are claimed, and the observer refuses to write through a cursor outside the test's own arena, which is what makes the deliberately-unmapped cursor of case F safe to drive. Four of the sixteen mutations are killed by SIGSEGV rather than by an assertion, so a run that faults has still refuted the reconstruction but has not reported which case did it; the four are listed above with the case that drives the fault.

validation.wpedantic_note: This package is NOT -Wpedantic-clean on GCC, and the cause is the prescribed calling-convention macro pattern itself rather than anything written here: GCC rejects `__attribute__((thiscall))` on a non-class free function under -Wattributes, which -Wpedantic promotes, so even a two-line file containing only the prescribed #define block and a free function declaration fails. The mandated gate does not enable -Wpedantic and passes clean. This is the same note pkg-dfw-006a2e20 records; some sidecars claim a -Wpedantic gate, and this one records the gate it actually ran.
